findings.evidence: The file has only three theorems, all `derivationComp ... = ...` equations. The torus results are in DiagonalTorus/GraphAutomorphism.lean (typeAGraphCoordinateIso_hom_comp_diagonalTorusCoordinateMap), which this file does not import. The pinning theorem's only assumptions are `[Nontrivial R] [ConnectedSpace (PrimeSpectrum R)]`.
findings.fix: Say what the file proves: the graph differential sends the standard pinning's chosen generator `i` to generator `i.rev` (same scalar) over any nontrivial base with connected spectrum. Drop the claim that it identifies the action on the pinning, and drop 'integral'.
findings.issue: Overclaim: 'Together with its torus and Borel preservation equations, this identifies its action on the standard integral pinning.' The file only proves three differential equations on chosen generators. It states no pinning-level transport and combines no torus/Borel results. 'Integral' is also wrong: the theorem holds over any nontrivial base with connected spectrum.

findings.evidence: Statement: LHS uses `standardPinningSimpleRootEquiv i` and RHS uses `standardPinningSimpleRootEquiv i.rev`, both with scalar `c`.
findings.fix: Reword to: 'The graph differential sends the standard pinning's simple-root trivialization at `i` and scalar `c` to the trivialization at `i.rev` with the same scalar `c`.'
findings.issue: The docstring 'preserves the scalar coordinates of every chosen simple-root trivialization' suggests each trivialization is fixed. The statement maps trivialization `i` at `c` to trivialization `i.rev` at `c`.

summary: The module docstring claims more than the file proves, and the pinning theorem's docstring leaves out the i ↦ i.rev reversal that the statement establishes.
